These tests were conducted under acceleration conditions involving wide open throttles. It was also assumed that even though the engine size is reduced the drivers will continue to accelerate at the same rate, all other conditions remaining the same. Testing in this manner will produce increases in noise levels because of increased engine RPM. However, these tests do not represent actual operating conditions which may effect the community. Plans are underway to develop noise standards for motor vanicles which will be more representative of their operation in communities. It is anticipated that reductions of engine size, resulting from this standard, will have an imperceptible effect on community noise levels.
